prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) coordinates incidents, dispatch, jurisdictional coverage, shared records and surge; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local-policy responsibility. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location, collects callback, symptoms/onset/access details, preserves original reports and separates facts from estimates; produces Caller Location Correction Slip and receives Bedside Arrival Receipt, verifying arrival time against dispatch/crew communications. Triage follows symptom/location/hazard capture and requires reassessment. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) resolves uncertainty, directs clarification without delaying urgent response, records priority/rationale/response level, sends Pediatric Acuity Note and validates surge declarations. Regional Medical Director sets clinical policy/priorities, advises specialty care/destinations, and guides non-routine demand/protocol adjustments; no dispatch authority. Pediatric airway, breathing, circulation or mental-status concerns get prompt approved-protocol escalation. Shift Commander (Sundial) manages readiness, surge/coverage, reviews coverage before moves, approves material coverage-reducing exceptions, sends Mutual Aid Release Form on neighboring-service release, reviews access affecting arrival/safe transfer and escalates unresolved destination/access issues. Paramedic Crew reports readiness/status, position, changes and route hazards; remains staged until relocation/direct assignment confirmed. Ambulance Unit 417 reports facility arrival and completed handover. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network reachability/backups, assignments, priority/routes and Coverage Gap Bulletin below threshold. Network carries dispatch/crew updates en route and destination instructions; crew acknowledges destination and requests renewed consultation if conditions warrant. Transmissions include incident ID, location, priority, assignment, hazards; crew repeats location/priority. Retry unacknowledged calls, correct discrepancies with fresh transmission; handoff requires acknowledgment and dispatch confirmation. North Gate Status Board shows northern queue/access; South Gate Status Board displays south-entrance access and produces South Access Lane Notice for material constraints. Juniper uses queue snapshot for northern routing, battery swap voucher before service, and compares projected response with remaining coverage before moves. Platform time-stamps changes; Data Quality Officer routes corrections and reviews incomplete arrival/handover fields. Emergency Department and crew resolve identity/transfer-document discrepancies before crew clears; Juniper updates incident status after confirmed transfer to facility care. Kestrel (Hospital Liaison Desk) coordinates capacity/preferences/constraints and consultation; confirms receiving capability, records outcomes/restrictions, informs Juniper, and supports handover questions. Destination decisions consider acuity, transport time, coverage and facility acceptance; Larkspur

New part:
S181: Call Taker Mara obtains the age, weight when available, and caregiver observations needed to support pediatric triage.
S182: Paramedic Crew reassesses pediatric patients during transport and reports material changes to the receiving facility.
S183: Kestrel shall confirm that facility capacity and pediatric service limitations are communicated to dispatch before a destination is finalized.
S184: Riverside Trauma Center advises Hospital Liaison Desk when trauma intake conditions may affect the suitability of an otherwise appropriate destination.
S185: Emergency Department staff acknowledge destination changes through the established coordination channel and identify any immediate access restrictions.
S186: Hospital Liaison Desk records facility responses in the regional coordination record and keeps dispatch informed of unresolved constraints.
S187: Mutual aid is requested when local staffed units cannot meet the declared response objectives or when a specialized resource is unavailable.
S188: Regional Radio Network carries mutual-aid requests, acceptance confirmations, and operational updates using the agreed regional call signs.
S189: Copperfield shall approve any temporary triage override and document its rationale before the override is applied.
S190: Ambulance Coordination Platform tracks accepted mutual-aid assignments separately from locally staffed resources to preserve an accurate coverage view.
S191: Ambulance Unit 417 may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms that its current patient-care and transport obligations permit the change.
S192: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports a vehicle restriction promptly so dispatch does not count an unavailable unit toward operational coverage.
S193: Triage Supervisor reviews the audit memo before closing a suspected duplicate incident.
S194: Data Quality Officer reviews unresolved record discrepancies through the established quality process without delaying active patient care.
S195: North Gate Status Board provides a current view of access conditions that may affect ambulance approach or handover timing.
S196: South Gate Status Board provides the equivalent access view for routes and entry points on the southern side of the region.
S197: After surge conditions ease, Shift Commander confirms that outstanding assignments, destination constraints, and staffing gaps have been handed over to the next operational period.
S198: Regional Dispatch Center maintains a degraded-radio procedure that prioritizes emergency traffic and preserves a common operating picture.
S199: Regional Radio Network operators announce channel outages, affected areas, and expected restoration times over the remaining service channels.
S200: Radio Coordinator directs crews to approved fallback channels when the primary channel is unusable.
S201: Crews acknowledge each fallback assignment and repeat critical location and destination details before moving.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
